title: Crash-Recoverable Saga with Exactly-Once Compensation
description: Orchestrate retries, crash recovery, and reverse-order compensation through a durable caller-owned journal.
prompt: Define exceptions `RetryableError`, `FatalError`, and `CrashError`, plus class `SagaOrchestrator(executor, compensator, max_retries: int = 2, journal: dict | None = None)`. `executor(step_name)` performs a step; `compensator(step_name)` undoes it. Implement `run(saga_id: str, steps: list[str]) -> str` and `recover(saga_id: str, steps: list[str]) -> str`. Steps must be unique non-empty strings. Persist progress in the caller-owned `journal` immediately after every successful action or compensation; expose that same object as `.journal`. A successful saga returns `completed`. Skip already completed steps after recovery. Retry `RetryableError` up to `max_retries` additional attempts; exhaustion is fatal. `FatalError` or exhausted retries trigger compensation of completed steps in reverse order, each exactly once, returning `compensated`. `CrashError` from either callback must propagate immediately without starting extra work; a later `recover` continues from durable progress. If recovery finds compensation in progress, it must resume compensation rather than execute forward steps. Reject a changed step plan for an existing saga. Callback exceptions other than the three declared exceptions are fatal. Validate before mutating the journal. Provide only valid Python code in one fenced block.
